title: FiniteDimensionalWeakMinty.lean

problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Unconstrained root finding for a globally L-Lipschitz operator F on ℝᵈ. The operator may be nonmonotone and satisfies a weak Minty inequality relative to a root.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: One query at any x ∈ ℝᵈ returns the full vector F(x) exactly for every history and oracle seed. The algorithm receives d, L, ρ, x₀, R, and ε as public inputs. It accesses F through queries, and the witnessing root is hidden.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/EuclideanWeakMinty.lean, Params and spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Query, spec.Reply, spec.admissible

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The domain and codomain are Euclidean ℝᵈ for every integer d ≥ 1. The valid parameter range is L > 0, 0 ≤ ρ ≤ 1/(20L), and 0 < ε < LR.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: A single root x⋆ satisfies F(x⋆) = 0, ‖x⋆ − x₀‖ ≤ R, and ⟨F(x), x − x⋆⟩ ≥ −ρ‖F(x)‖² for every x ∈ ℝᵈ.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The residual norm must be integrable and satisfy 𝔼‖F(X)‖ ≤ ε under the product law of the algorithm and oracle seeds. The query budget is fixed, and the algorithm may randomize.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/EuclideanWeakMinty.lean, spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean, executeWithTrace and Convergence

accuracy.label: other
accuracy.details: The algorithm outputs a point X ∈ ℝᵈ. Accuracy is measured by the unsquared Euclidean residual norm ‖F(X)‖. The output may be any point, including one the algorithm has not queried.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/EuclideanWeakMinty.lean, spec.Output and spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean, Algorithm.output

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The weak Minty condition allows the operator to point away from the witnessing root, with the inner-product violation bounded by ρ times the squared residual norm.

descriptionHtml:
Finite-Dimensional Weak Minty Root Finding

We seek an approximate zero of a Lipschitz operator F:Rd→Rd in dimension d≥1. A given starting point x0∈Rd lies within a prescribed radius of a zero x⋆ at which F satisfies the weak Minty condition. The oracle returns F(x) at any query point x∈Rd. For a tolerance ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈Rd with integrable Euclidean residual norm satisfying E[∥F(x¯)∥]≤ε, where the expectation is over the algorithm’s randomness.

The underlying equation is F(x)=0,x∈Rd. We use the Euclidean inner product and its induced norm. The algorithm receives d, x0, the Lipschitz constant L, the weak Minty parameter ρ, the radius R, and the tolerance ε, with d∈{1,2,…},L>0,0≤ρ≤120L,0<ε<LR.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Lipschitz continuity). For all x,y∈Rd, ∥F(x)−F(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥.

Assumption 2 (Weak Minty condition at a nearby zero). There exists x⋆∈Rd with F(x⋆)=0 and ∥x⋆−x0∥≤R such that, for every x∈Rd, ⟨F(x),x−x⋆⟩≥−ρ∥F(x)∥2.

After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must satisfy ∥F(x¯)∥∈L1(P),EP[∥F(x¯)∥]≤ε, where P is the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

comparisonHtml:
An exact query returns F(x) for an L-Lipschitz map F:Rd→Rd, d≥1, L>0. Some root z satisfies ∥z−x0∥≤R and ⟨F(x),x−z⟩≥−ρ∥F(x)∥2 for all x, with 0≤ρL≤1/20. The target is an integrable residual with ∫∥F(x^(ω))∥dP(ω)≤ε for 0<ε<LR, where P is the execution law. Rows (1) and (2) match in order for this oracle and criterion.

Exact-oracle residual bounds for finite-dimensional weak-Minty problems.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) DimensionAdaptiveMintyLowerBound (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) Necessary budget Ω(H) for randomized adaptive queries. Hard instances satisfy plain Minty.
(2) DimensionAdaptiveMinty (Ours) (⋆⋆) (review) Sufficient budget O(H), counting two evaluations per step.
(3) Upper bound. Derived bound using EG+ and look-ahead centroid cuts (Diakonikolas et al. 2021; Anagnostides et al. 2026) Sufficient budget O(min{t2,d(1+log⁡t)}). Same residual target and weak-Minty range. (2): At d≍t2/log⁡t, O(t2log⁡log⁡t/log⁡t) instead of O(t2). The maximum order gain is log⁡t/log⁡log⁡t as t→∞. Same order for d≤t2−δ with fixed δ>0.
(4) Upper bound. EG+ (Diakonikolas et al. 2021, Thm. 3.2) Sufficient budget O(t2/(1−8ρL)) for ρL<1/8. (2): On the common range, bound improves by order t2/H when d≤t2, with a growing gain for d=o(t2). Matches the known rate for d≥t2. (2): Smaller ρL range, requires global Minty inequality and exact centroid integration for cuts. EG+ uses linear arithmetic per step.
(5) Lower bound. Lipschitz Minty (auto-math-bot 2026) Necessary budget Ω(min{t2,d1/3}) for randomized adaptive queries. (1): All d≥1, t>1 instead of d≥257, t≥28. On overlap, improves by order H/d1/3 for d≤t2 and t2/d1/3 for t2≤d≤t6. Same order for d≥t6. (1): Smaller leading constant. Its stated failure budget reaches one call only when H≥222.
(6) Lower bound. Biaffine saddle gradients (Yoon and Ryu 2021, Thm. 4) Necessary budget Ω(t) for deterministic queries in dimension d≳t. (1): Covers randomized adaptive queries and all dimensions on the broader Minty class, with Ω(t2) for d≥t2. The rates concern different classes. (1): The hard fields are outside the saddle-gradient subclass.
(7) Lower bound. Compact-interval Minty gap (Anagnostides et al. 2026, Cor. 6.9) Necessary budget Ω(η−1/4) for gap η, at constant success probability, on [0,1] with L=O(η1/2) and supx∥F(x)∥=O(η3/4). (1): Rates are incomparable because the compact-domain guarantee concerns a global Minty gap.

Abbr: t=LR/ε, H=dlog⁡(1+t2/d). Gap η means ⟨F(y),y−x^⟩≥−η for all feasible y.

import LongTails.Setups.EuclideanWeakMinty

namespace LongTails.Setups.FiniteDimensionalWeakMinty

open OracleTemplate

abbrev Params := EuclideanWeakMinty.Params

abbrev spec : Setup := { EuclideanWeakMinty.spec with
  valid := fun p => 0 < p.d ∧ 0 < p.L ∧ 0 ≤ p.ρ ∧ p.ρ ≤ 1 / (20 * p.L) ∧
    0 < p.ε ∧ p.ε < p.L * p.R }

end LongTails.Setups.FiniteDimensionalWeakMinty
